messages:
alex: Heads up — since we enabled mixed-instance spot pools yesterday we've seen a weird pattern: some GPU workloads fail to schedule with OOM-like errors and others get evicted mid-run. Not full outages but lots of retries.

marta: Noted. Any logs? Is this happening across regions or just us-east-1?

alex: Mainly us-east-1. I grabbed kube-scheduler + kubelet logs from one affected node. Looks like pods request `nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5` (fractional via MIG/time-slice) and the node reports available GPUs but kubelet rejects due to device plugin not reporting the exact fractional topology. Error: \"no matching devices: requested 512MB cache?\" — weird.

kai: Are these using the GPU sharing CRI plugin we deployed (v0.7)? We pushed a config yesterday that changes reported topology for 1g/2g MIG slices. Could be a mismatch between device plugin and scheduler predicates.

jordan: Also saw increased scale-down churn in the autoscaler logs around the same time. CA tried to drain nodes, then pods couldn't fit into remaining nodes because of fragmented MIG assignments, so CA canceled scale-down. That explains the retries.

alex: Here's a snippet of the failing pod request (simplified):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: trainer-fractional
spec:
  containers:
  - name: train
    image: our-train:latest
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "8"
        memory: "32Gi"
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.5"
```

marta: Thanks. Two immediate suspects: 1) device plugin reports fractional units differently after the upgrade, 2) autoscaler drain/scale-down timing + PodDisruptionBudget interplay causing temporary packing failures. What does `kubectl describe node` show for allocatable GPUs?

alex: On one node: Allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu=2 (but device plugin lists 4 MIG slices as separate resources). The scheduler tries to pack one `0.5` request into a MIG slice already partially used and fails.

kai: That suggests the device plugin is advertising slices but without the topology annotations scheduler predicates expect. We recently toggled `--enable-gpu-topology=true` in the plugin config. Maybe older scheduler predicate was relying on topology manager.

jordan: Autoscaler note: CA v1.28 has a scale-down-unneeded-time set to 10m in the new profile; before it was 20m. Lowering it made CA more aggressive, which exacerbated fragmentation.

marta: Proposed mitigation (short term): revert plugin flag to previous behavior and increase CA scale-down-unneeded-time back to 20m, plus add a temporary taint on the spot MIG pool so only tolerant workloads land there. That buys time.

kai: Agreed. Also add a scheduler Extender rule to prefer packing fractional requests onto nodes with matching free MIG slices. We can implement a simple priority in the extender that reads device plugin annotations.

alex: I'll roll the plugin revert to canary pool and bump the CA setting. Can someone craft the taint + toleration for user jobs? We should auto-assign lower-priority batch jobs to the spot pool.

jordan: I'll handle the taint. Suggest: `kubectl taint nodes -l pool=spot-mig spot-mig=true:NoSchedule` and add toleration to our batch job template. Also adding `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` was causing some evictions; check that while you roll.

marta: Longer-term: 1) formalize a GPU packing heuristic in scheduler (pack fractional onto same MIG until threshold), 2) update device plugin contract: advertise fractional units consistently, 3) CA should be aware of MIG fragmentation (avoid scale-down that increases fragmentation). I'll open RFC.

alex: Sounds good. I'll post a short incident follow-up once the canary is stable. For now: revert plugin flag, increase CA timeout, taint spot pool.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollback of gpu-plugin config started on nodepool=cana ry at 1861234575 — 3/4 nodes updated, health checks passing.

kai: After revert we should run a synthetic schedule test: 100 pods requesting 0.5 GPU across 10 nodes and verify packing + no evictions. I can script that.

jordan: Logged: ENGINFRA-482 to track RFC + mitigation steps.

marta: Great. Keep updates short in thread. If rollback fixes it we can do wider rollout. :thumbsup:
